items.title: Building AI Evaluations You Can Actually Trust - Tejas Kumar
items.author: DataTalksClub ⬛
items.summary:
In this talk Tejas Kumar AI Engineer at IBM shares his journey from experimenting with early image generation models as an enthusiast to deploying enterprise grade coding agents. We explore the critical practice of building reliable AI evaluations the LLM as a judge architecture and why manual vibe checking is no longer enough to secure production LLM applications.

Links: 
- AI Evals: How to Build an LLM Judge That Agrees With You - https://tej.as/blog/ai-evals-llm-judge
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C_GG5g38vLU
- Evals code, demos, and slides - https://github.com/TejasQ/basically-agent-evals
- Tejas's Book, Fluent React: https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/fluent-react/9781098138707/

You will learn about:
- The exact definition of the modern AI Engineer and how it differs from traditional machine learning roles
- Why high profile AI agent failures happen like the Meta customer support hack and how proper evaluations prevent them
- How to source data and build a comprehensive golden dataset for testing non deterministic LLM outputs
- Implementing the LLM as a judge architecture to evaluate generative AI agents accurately at scale
- The eighty five percent rule for successfully aligning automated AI judges with human quality standards
- Managing high severity edge cases using closed hand evaluations that strictly block dangerous or off policy outputs
- Why you should separate your execution harness testing from your core agent evaluations

TIMECODES:
00:00 Defining AI Engineering
12:11 The Importance of AI Evals and Safety
18:54 How to Build a Comprehensive Eval Set
24:57 Sourcing Data and Creating a Golden Dataset
30:45 High Severity Scenarios and Closed Hand Evals
36:26 Aligning AI Judges with Human Standards
42:45 Using Evals for Security and Reliability
48:52 Primary vs Secondary Metrics in Evals
55:00 Updating Judges and Human Labeling Methods
01:01:12 Separating Harness Tests from Agent Evals

This discussion is tailored for software developers data scientists and emerging AI engineers looking to transition generative AI applications from prototype to production. It provides actionable frameworks for technical teams tasked with ensuring the security reliability and accuracy of customer facing AI agents.
